1.s: agnirindraḥ prajāpatiḥ somo varuṇastvaṣṭāṅgirasaḥ pūṣā sarasvatīndrāgnī |
1.d: अग्निरिन्द्रः प्रजापतिः सोमो वरुणस्त्वष्टाङ्गिरसः पूषा सरस्वतीन्द्राग्नी ।
1.m: Agni, Indra, Prajāpati, Soma, Varuṇa, Tvaṣṭṛ, the Aṅgirases, Pūṣan, Sarasvatī, Indrāgnī.
Those [sāmans] with an iḍā-finale, those with a pada-finale, and those with an i-sound-finale belong to Agni.
All [sāmans] possessing a finale are Indra's, other than those specifically designated.
All [sāmans] ending in a tone belong to Prajāpati;
Those with the finale 'vāc' belong to Varuṇa;
Those whose tone follows the syllable belong to Tvaṣṭṛ;
as, for example, the Vāravantīya and the Ābhīvarta.
Those with 'svaḥ' as the back belong to the Aṅgirases.
Those with 'svaḥ' as a finale belong to Pūṣan.

1.s: kayā naścitra ā bhuvad ā pavasva sahasriṇam iti vāṅanidhane sārasvate |
1.d: कया नश्चित्र आ भुवद् आ पवस्व सहस्रिणम् इति वाङनिधने सारस्वते ।
1.m: [The sāmans on the verses] 'By what splendid aid will he be present for us...' and 'Flow on, thou that bringest a thousandfold...', having 'vāc' as a finale, belong to Sarasvatī.
[and] 'Being in wealth, the pressed [soma]... being in wealth, the strength...', belong to Indrāgnī.
The Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, the Viśvedevas.

1.s: vasūnāṃ svārāṇi rudrāṇāṃ nidhanavanti ādityānāmaiḍāni viśveṣāṃ devānāṃ vāṅnidhanāni |
1.d: वसूनां स्वाराणि रुद्राणां निधनवन्ति आदित्यानामैडानि विश्वेषां देवानां वाङ्निधनानि ।
1.m: Those ending in a tone belong to the Vasus; those possessing a finale belong to the Rudras; those with an iḍā belong to the Ādityas; those with 'vāc' as a finale belong to the Viśvedevas.
Because statements apply predominantly [in this way], these are the closer [attributions].

1.s: athāntaratarāṇi sarvāṇyāgneyani sarvāṇyaindrāṇi sarvāṇi svārāṇi prājāpatyāni sāmanītyantaratarāṇi |
1.d: अथान्तरतराणि सर्वाण्याग्नेयनि सर्वाण्यैन्द्राणि सर्वाणि स्वाराणि प्राजापत्यानि सामनीत्यन्तरतराणि ।
1.m: Now the still closer: all sāmans belong to Agni, all belong to Indra, all sāmans ending in a tone belong to Prajāpati—these are the still closer.
Now the innermost: all sāmans belong to Brahman—these are the innermost of all.

1.s: ṛgvai mātā sāma pitā prajāpatiḥ svaraḥ |
1.d: ऋग्वै माता साम पिता प्रजापतिः स्वरः ।
1.m: The verse indeed is the mother; the sāman is the father; the tone is Prajāpati.

1.s: atha yānyṛkta ākhyāyante mātṛtastānyānyākhyāyante atha yāni sāmata ākhyāyante pitṛtastānyākhyāyante atha yāni svarata ākhyāyante prajāpatitastānyākhyāyante |
1.d: अथ यान्यृक्त आख्यायन्ते मातृतस्तान्यान्याख्यायन्ते अथ यानि सामत आख्यायन्ते पितृतस्तान्याख्यायन्ते अथ यानि स्वरत आख्यायन्ते प्रजापतितस्तान्याख्यायन्ते ।

1.s: sa vā eṣa udgītho bandhumān bandhumatyaḥ |
1.d: स वा एष उद्गीथो बन्धुमान् बन्धुमत्यः ।
1.m: Indeed, this udgītha has kin, has female kin.

1.s: bandhumān bandhumatyo bhavati jānanti ha vā enaṃ pitṛtaśca mātṛtaśca ya evaṃ deva |
1.d: बन्धुमान् बन्धुमत्यो भवति जानन्ति ह वा एनं पितृतश्च मातृतश्च य एवं देव ।
1.m:
He comes to have kin, to have female kin;

they know him both from the father's side and from the mother's side,

2.m: Now, therefore, the colours of the metres:

2.s: śuklā gāyatryo rūpeṇa sāraṅgaṃ rūpamuṣṇihām piśaṅgaṃ kakubhāṃ rūpaṃ kṛṣṇamānuṣṭubhaṃ tataḥ | rohitaṃ bṛhītāṃ tu nīlaṃ pāṅktaṃ tataḥ punaḥ suvarṇa triṣṭubhāṃ rūpaṃ gauraṃ jāgatamucyate |
2.d: शुक्ला गायत्र्यो रूपेण सारङ्गं रूपमुष्णिहाम् पिशङ्गं ककुभां रूपं कृष्णमानुष्टुभं ततः । रोहितं बृहीतां तु नीलं पाङ्क्तं ततः पुनः सुवर्ण त्रिष्टुभां रूपं गौरं जागतमुच्यते ।

2.s: atho yānyanyāni cchandāṃsi śyāvaṃ teṣāṃ tataḥ punaḥ nakulaṃ tvekapadānāṃ dvipadā babhrurucyate sāraṅgaśuklakṛṣṇarūpāṇi ṛgyajuḥsāmabrāhmaṇānvitāni |
2.d: अथो यान्यन्यानि च्छन्दांसि श्यावं तेषां ततः पुनः नकुलं त्वेकपदानां द्विपदा बभ्रुरुच्यते सारङ्गशुक्लकृष्णरूपाणि ऋग्यजुःसामब्राह्मणान्वितानि ।

2.m: The deity of those that are to be employed in the sacrifices is declared.
One should know the Virājs to be dappled.

2.s: agnergāyatryabhavatsayugvoṣṇihayā savitā saṃbhabhūvānuṣṭubhā soma ukthairmahasvān bṛhaspaterbṛhatī vācamāvat |
2.d: अग्नेर्गायत्र्यभवत्सयुग्वोष्णिहया सविता संभभूवानुष्टुभा सोम उक्थैर्महस्वान् बृहस्पतेर्बृहती वाचमावत् ।
2.m: Gāyatrī became united with Agni; Savitṛ came into being together with Uṣṇih; Soma, radiant through songs of praise, with Anuṣṭubh; Bṛhatī fostered the speech of Bṛhaspati;

2.s: virāṇmitrāvaruṇayorabhiśrīr indrasya triṣṭubiha bhāgo ahnaḥ viśvān devān jagatyāviveśa tena cakḷpta ṛṣayo manuṣyāḥ |
2.d: विराण्मित्रावरुणयोरभिश्रीर् इन्द्रस्य त्रिष्टुबिह भागो अह्नः विश्वान् देवान् जगत्याविवेश तेन चकॢप्त ऋषयो मनुष्याः ।
2.m:
Virāj was the ornament of Mitra and Varuṇa; Triṣṭubh was Indra's share here by day;

Jagatī entered the Viśvedevas; thereby were the ṛṣis and mortals arranged.

2.s: prājāpatyā aticchandaso vicchandaso vāyudevatāḥ puruṣo dvipadānaṃ daivataṃ brāhmya ekapadāḥ smṛtāḥ |
2.d: प्राजापत्या अतिच्छन्दसो विच्छन्दसो वायुदेवताः पुरुषो द्विपदानं दैवतं ब्राह्म्य एकपदाः स्मृताः ।
2.m:
The hyper-metres belong to Prajāpati; the defective metres have Vāyu as their deity;

Puruṣa is the deity of the two-line [metres]; the single-line [metres] are remembered as belonging to Brahman.
One should consider it balanced [saying]: 'Verses in these metres have these very deities.'
This indeed is the deity of the metres.

3.m: 'Gāyatrī' is from [the root] gāi, in the sense of praising;
for the Brāhmaṇa says: 'It flew up from the mouth of him singing.'
'Uṣṇih' is from rising out of water (utsnāna), or from snih in the sense of shining or being affectionate, or it is metaphorical, meaning 'possessing a turban' (uṣṇīṣiṇī).
'Kakubh' is metaphorical, meaning 'possessing the shape of a peak' (kakuda).
And both 'kakubh' and 'kubja' (hump-backed) are from kuj or from ubj (to bend).
for the Brāhmaṇa says: 'He praised along after [it].'
'Pipīlikā' (ant) is from pel in the sense of moving;
'having an ant-waist' (pipīlikamadhyā) is metaphorical.
'Bṛhatī' is from bṛh in the sense of growing.
The virāj [is so called] from ceasing (viramaṇa), from shining forth (virājana), or from failing (virādhana).
The paṅkti has five [units] (pañcinī), having five feet (pañcapadā).
The triṣṭubh: its last foot praises (stobhati).

3.s: kā tu tritā syāttirṇatamaṃ chando bhavatīti |
3.d: का तु त्रिता स्यात्तिर्णतमं छन्दो भवतीति ।
3.m: What, however, could its threefoldness (tritā) be? It is the metre that has crossed over most (tīrṇatama).
The thunderbolt is threefold; it is like its praiser (stobhinī)—thus by way of comparison.
The jagatī is the metre that moves most (gatatama); it becomes moving swiftly (jajjagati), swift in movement.
For a Brāhmaṇa says: 'Making the sound jajjalā, he created.'
The aticchandas metres are [derived] in the sense of covering (chad).
Or [they are so called because] it covers (chandayati) the metres.
Nicṛt [is] from the [root] cṛt preceded by ni; from bearing (bharaṇa), it is called bhurij.

3.s: athāto gāyatramāgneyaṃ bhaktyā bhavati devānāṃ varṣiṇāṃ vā parameṣṭino vā prājāpatyasya sāma |
3.d: अथातो गायत्रमाग्नेयं भक्त्या भवति देवानां वर्षिणां वा परमेष्टिनो वा प्राजापत्यस्य साम ।
3.m:
Now then, the gāyatra [sāman] belongs to Agni by distribution,

or to the deities of rain, or [it is] the sāman of Parameṣṭhin or of Prajāpati.
Where it is sung as to be sung to Savitṛ:

He who knows the realm of the ṛṣis is released from the body;

having crossed beyond the far shore of darkness, he is exalted in the heavenly world.

What is called a day of Brahmā, ending in a thousand yugas—

for that duration, he shines on the back of the firmament like the sun in the sky.

Then, at the beginning of the Kṛta Yuga, having become Brahman, of great renown,

omniscient, steadfast, the ṛṣi is born again, remembering.

4.s: atha sāvitryaṅgāni vyākhyāsyāmaḥ śiro brahmā lalāṭaṃ dyauḥ candrādityau cakṣuṣi mukhamagniḥ jihvā sarasvatī tvaṣṭā grīvā vasavaśca rudrāśca bāhū uro vāyuḥ romāṇi vāyavaḥ | pṛṣṭhindraḥ viṣṇurnābhiḥ prajāpatirjaghanam ūrū marutaḥ devāḥ pādau smitaṃ vidyut śvasitaṃ vāyuḥ asthīni parvatāḥ samudrā vāsāṃsi nakṣatrāṇi alaṃtrāṇi alaṃkāraḥ |
4.d: अथ सावित्र्यङ्गानि व्याख्यास्यामः शिरो ब्रह्मा ललाटं द्यौः चन्द्रादित्यौ चक्षुषि मुखमग्निः जिह्वा सरस्वती त्वष्टा ग्रीवा वसवश्च रुद्राश्च बाहू उरो वायुः रोमाणि वायवः । पृष्ठिन्द्रः विष्णुर्नाभिः प्रजापतिर्जघनम् ऊरू मरुतः देवाः पादौ स्मितं विद्युत् श्वसितं वायुः अस्थीनि पर्वताः समुद्रा वासांसि नक्षत्राणि अलंत्राणि अलंकारः ।
4.m:
Now we shall explain the limbs of the Sāvitrī:

the Vasus and Rudras are the two arms;
the lunar mansions are the ornaments, the decoration.
well-being from all defect, misuse, deficiency, and excess!

4.d: ब्रह्म सत्यं च पातु मामिति । ब्रह्म सत्यं च पातु मामिति ।
4.m:
'May Brahman and truth protect me.'

'May Brahman and truth protect me.'
